the native geothermally active brine is present in the reservoir at Soultz, but that it is not in a large volume.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
, at the Soultz-s-s-F site, the native geothermal fluids are of sedimentary origin and are equilibrated at high temperatures with a mineralogic assemblage situated in a sedimentary reservoir.
the geochemical data and tracer tests provide a good understanding of the origin, nature and circulation of the native geothermally heated fluids at Soultz.
the Soultz geothermal system appears to be a very promising one, but the exploitation of this resource is still limited by the low permeability and hydraulic conductivity of the reservoir.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the geochemical data are very useful in understanding the origin of the geothermal fluids and in characterizing the fluid flow in deep geothermal systems, even if the geochemical analyses are not representative of the deep reservoir.
the native geothermals fluids, which are of sedimentary origin, are still the dominant fluids in the Soultz HDR reservoir, despite the large amounts of water injected into the wells since 1995.

, despite the high temperature and the large depth of this HDR site, the geothermal fluid is a NaCl brine of sedimentary origin, with a temperature of 220-240oC, and a salinity of 100 g/l, which is very close to that of the geothermal fluids produced at the surface in the Rhine Graban (Sanjuan et. al., 2005 and 2006a).
